title: Valid Sudoku
description: Check each row, column, and 3×3 square for repeated digits, ignoring empty cells.
note: Assume a 9×9 board containing digits 1–9 or '.'. Validity concerns the filled cells; it does not require a completed or solvable board.
notes: Birdie represents each cell as char. Python represents the same cells as one-character strings. Both examples use the same helper, extracted variables, and check order, with the main algorithm first and validGroup below it.

validGroup captures no enclosing variables, so it is a separate function. Birdie registers function declarations before ordinary execution, allowing the main function to call a helper written later. The Python helper is also top-level and is defined before the judge invokes the main method.
for i until 9 starts at zero and excludes nine. Adding step 3 visits square origins 0, 3, and 6. Nonzero starts remain explicit in the square comprehension.
List comprehensions eagerly collect a column or square. Multiple for clauses run like nested loops and produce a flat list. Their bindings do not leak into the enclosing function.
Each call to validGroup creates a fresh set[char]. continue skips empty cells, and the first repeated digit makes the group invalid. None of the checks modifies the input board.
Each of the 81 cells is examined in its row, column, and square unless validation returns early. Work and auxiliary storage are bounded for the fixed 9×9 board.
